before: Wesley taught three things that later mattered for Pentecostals. First, entire sanctification is a gift received by faith, not earned by works. Second, it may be received in a moment, not only after a long struggle. Third, it normally comes after conversion, as a second, definite experience. He set out these ideas in his book *A Plain Account of Christian Perfection* (1766). Wesley's close associate John Fletcher of Madeley used the language of the "baptism of the Spirit" when he spoke about this deeper work. This is an important link. Years before Azusa Street, Methodists were already connecting a second experience of grace with the Holy Spirit's coming.

before: Methodism grew quickly in North America. Its traveling preachers reached frontier settlements where there were few churches. Around 1800, in a time often called the Second Great Awakening, large outdoor gatherings called camp meetings became common. One of the best known took place at Cane Ridge, Kentucky, in 1801. People came from many miles, camped for days, and heard preaching, prayed and sought God. Observers wrote of deep repentance and also of unusual physical responses, which some leaders found troubling. What matters for our story is the pattern: ordinary believers gathered, prayed with expectation and looked for the Holy Spirit to move. The camp meeting remained part of Holiness and Pentecostal life for a century.

The evangelist Charles Finney (1792-1875) also taught that believers should seek a baptism of the Holy Spirit for power in service. He taught at Oberlin in Ohio, and the "Oberlin" teaching reached many churches. So the phrase "baptism of the Holy Spirit" was already used, in some circles, for an experience after conversion that brings power and purity.

before: One of its most influential leaders was a woman, Phoebe Palmer (1807-1874) of New York. In 1835 she began a weekly "Tuesday Meeting for the Promotion of Holiness." Ministers and laypeople came to pray and testify. In her book *The Way of Holiness* (1843) she taught that a believer who lays everything on the altar of consecration, trusting the promise of God, may receive the blessing now and need not wait for a long period of seeking. Palmer's teaching made the experience feel close and available.

In 1867 a National Camp Meeting Association for the Promotion of Holiness held its first meeting at Vineland, New Jersey, and Holiness camp meetings multiplied. Some Methodists who felt unwelcome in their churches formed new bodies, such as the Free Methodist Church (1860). By the end of the century a large network of Holiness churches, missions, schools and periodicals existed.
after: One of its most influential leaders was a woman, Phoebe Palmer (1807-1874) of New York. In her book *The Way of Holiness* (1843) she taught that a believer who lays everything on the altar of consecration, trusting the promise of God, may receive the blessing now and need not wait for a long period of seeking. Palmer's teaching made the experience feel close and available. [U2.4]

before: A second stream of teaching came from the Keswick movement. In 1875, after meetings led by the American Quaker couple Robert Pearsall Smith and Hannah Whitall Smith, a convention was held at Keswick in the English Lake District. The convention continued yearly and influenced Christians in Britain, America and many mission fields.
after: A second stream of teaching came from the Keswick movement. The first Keswick Convention met in 1875 in the English Lake District, organized by Canon T. D. Harford-Battersby and Robert Wilson. It drew on the wider Higher Life movement, which had been promoted in Britain and North America by teachers including Robert Pearsall Smith and Hannah Whitall Smith. The annual convention became an important channel for Keswick teaching in Britain, North America, and mission fields. [U2.6]

In the 1800s, in Europe and America, a number of ministers began to teach that healing is provided in the atonement and that believers may pray for the sick with faith. ## Review and Reflection
1. How did Wesleyan-Holiness and Keswick teaching differ on sanctification and Spirit empowerment?
2. What did Phoebe Palmer contribute to Holiness teaching and practice?
3. Name one way an honest pastor can pray for healing while avoiding blame when healing does not occur.
